paper.title: Leveraging recurrence in neural network wavefunctions for large-scale simulations of Heisenberg antiferromagnets on the square lattice
paper.authors: M. Schuyler Moss, Roeland Wiersema, Mohamed Hibat-Allah, Juan Carrasquilla, Roger G. Melko

results.system_description: Heisenberg, 6 × 6 · J = 1 · periodic · Sz = 0. H = J sum_<ij> S_i · S_j; spin-1/2 operators S = sigma/2; J = 1; no constant shift
results.variant: best RNN (GRU cells, C4v and U(1) symmetric)
results.source_location: Appendix C, Table "Neural quantum state results for the SLAHM" (tab:nqs_energies), periodic 6 x 6, row "This work (best RNN)"
results.eligibility_evidence: Best variational energy per site of the 2D recurrent neural network state (bold "This work (best RNN)" rows); the zero-variance rows of the same table are extrapolations and are excluded.
results.notes: Heisenberg model H = sum S_i S_j (Eq. 1) with spin-1/2 operators; U(1) symmetry (Sz = 0) and C4v lattice symmetries are enforced (Sec. Methods and training table).

results.system_description: Heisenberg, 8 × 8 · J = 1 · open · Sz = 0. H = J sum_<ij> S_i · S_j; spin-1/2 operators S = sigma/2; J = 1; no constant shift
results.variant: best RNN (GRU cells, C4v and U(1) symmetric), training schedule s = 4.0, r = 0.475
results.source_location: Authors' data release github.com/mschuylermoss/HeisenbergRNN, commit 29bf62ac28, file Square/final_plotting/final_data/final_energy_data_plotting.pkl, entry ['open']['rate=0.475']['scale=4.0'], L = 8 (energies, std errors); plotted in Fig. fig:energy_variance_open(a)
results.eligibility_evidence: Final variational energy per site of the 2D RNN (estimated with 10^4 samples, caption of fig:energies_peri), plotted in Fig. fig:energy_variance_open(a) and printed only in the data release named in the Code Availability section. Of the training schedules in the file, the one with the lowest energy among those with scale s >= 1 is taken, the rule that reproduces the four 'This work (best RNN)' values of Table V (L = 6 and 10); the zero-variance extrapolations of Table III are excluded.
results.notes: Rounded to one significant digit of the standard error, as in Table V; the file holds E/N = -0.619034469127655 with standard error 5.7981170573067555e-06. The uncertainty is the file's 'std errors' entry. Marshall-Peierls sign rule, U(1) (Sz = 0) and C4v symmetries as for the paper's printed rows. The file also lists a variance; it is not recorded because its normalization is not stated.
